MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  JANUARY 8, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

  MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart called the meeting to order at 5:31 pm.

  ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Steve Uhring (arrived 5:45 p.m.); Mayor Pro Tem Doug Stewart; and
  Councilmembers Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Bruce Silverstein

  PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: None.

[j  RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 5:32 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss'the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

  Conference with Legal Counsel — Existing litigation pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(1):

  Case Name: City’s Petition to Form Malibu USD from'Territory in the Santa
  Monica-Malibu USD

  REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Uhring called the meeting to order at 6:48 p.m.

  ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Steve Uhring; Mayor Pro Tem Doug Stewart; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Bruce Silverstein

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attomey; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey
  Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Susan Duefias, Public
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 8, 2024
  Page 2 of 12

  Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Parker Davis, Media Technician;
  Christina Munoz, Deputy City Clerk; and Adrian Fernandez, Assistant Planning Director

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Norm Haynie led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 5:30 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(1). He stated Mayor Uhringjoined the meeting at approximately 5:45 p.m. He
  stated the Council discussed the items on the Closed Session agenda and took no reportable
  action.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  December 21, 2023, with the amended agenda posted on January 4, 2024.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda and adjourn in memory of Ray Humphrey and Lyon Herron.

FIRENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Stewart moved to hearing Item No. 6.C. before Item No. 6.B.

  The Council discussed the amendment.

  The maker and seconder of the motion accepted the amendment.

  The question was called, and the amended motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRE SENTATIONS

  A.  Presentation on Southern California Edison Updates

  Andrew Thomas, Southern California Edison (SCE) Government Relations
  Manager, presented on recent public safety power shutoff (PSPS) events and
  communication tools. John Morehouse, SCE, had technical difficulties and was
  unable to present.

  The Council directed questions to Mr. Thomas.

ITEM 6  NEW BUSINESS
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 8, 2024
  Page 3 of 12

  Road Race Agreement
  Recommended Action: At the recommendation of the Road Race Ad Hoc
  Committee, approve the Agreements with Malibu Race Series LLC and Zuma
  Foundation Inc. for the two allowable Road Race Temporary Use Permits.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  Mayor Uhring announced that, due to the number of speakers, each speaker would
  have two minutes to speak.

  Mayor Uhring opened the floor to public comment.

  Speaker: Jim Duncan, Elizabeth Rodrigues, Meril May, Linda Rooney, Pamela
  Conley Ulich, Merlin Clarke, Michael Epstein, Eric Gilseman, Keith Simmons,
  Nick Angio, Kasey Earnest, Cassidy Case, Erica Segel (Scott Brockwa deferred
  time to Ms. Segel), Ben Dewitt, Marty O’Malio, Robyn Simon, Jo Drummond,
  Veronica Hoomani, Maksym Shepitko, Tony Mark, Mikke Pierson, Brennan
  Lindner (Tim Bomba, Jake Ralph, and Paul Hekimian deferred time to Mr.
  Lindner), Heather Wildman, Lara Weberling, Robert Laurita, Teri Brown, Bill
  Sampson, Valentina, Tanvir H., and Rosa O’Reilly

  Christian Markey was not present at the time of the hearing.

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Uhring returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to the Road Race Ad Hoc
  Committee, Mr. Epstein, Mr. Lindner, Ms. Segel, and Mr. Angio.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved to: 1) approve the agreement with Zuma
  Foundation Inc., amending Sections 6.6 and 6.9 as presented, and 2) approve an
  agreement with Malibu Moves, amending Sections 6.6 and 6.9 as presented.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart seconded the motion and moved to amend Section 6.6 to
  direct the donation to “Malibu youth based 501(c)(3) organizations” and revert
  section 6.9 for the Zuma Foundation Inc. agreement.

  The maker accepted the amendment.

  The Council discussed the motion and directed questions to Ms. Case.

  Councilmember Silverstein withdrew the motion to consider the two agreements
  separately.

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Stewart seconded a motion
  to approve the agreement with Zuma Foundation Inc., amending Section 6.6. The

  question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.
MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Stewart seconded a motion
  to approve an agreement with Malibu Moves, amending Sections 6.6 and 6.9, and
  direct staff to make any further changes to form as recommended by the City
  Attorney and approved by the City Manager. The question was called, and the
  motion carried 4-1, Councilmember Riggins opposed.

RECESS  At 9:26 p.m., Mayor Uhring recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 9:38
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.
ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Meril May thanked the City for the increased presence of law enforcement on
  Pacific Coast Highway (PCH). He recommended the City advertise upcoming
  Caltrans projects and warn motorists to drive carefully. He stated speed cameras
  were the next step for PCH safety. He stated palm trees across from HRL posed a
  fire hazard. He discussed the December 21, 2024 Tesla crash at Busch Drive.

  Scott Dittrich discussed the SCE presentation and recent PSPS events.

  Jo Drummond stated the City should focus on safety and the environment. She
  recommended the Council direct staffto focus on the permanent skate park project,
  getting the communicatiOns tower at the SMC Malibu Campus lowered and
  camouflaged, lowering permit fees for small projects, prioritizing like-for—like fire
  rebuilds, developing recreation facilities on the City’s vacant land, removing fire
  hazards, and undergrounding utilities. She recommended having a potluck at City
  Council meetings.

  Andy Lyon discussed the appeal of the Coastal Development Permit (CDP) for the
  permanent skate park. He recommended the Council deny the appeal and approve
  the project as proposed.

  Colin Drummond stated he intended to speak on Item No. 7.A.

  Tamikofuote discussed the importance of controlling speeding on PCH.  She
  discussed her husband’s death on PCH.

  Kraig Hill stated he intended to speak on Item No. 7.A.

  Ryan Embree was not available at the time of the hearing.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  City Manager McClary stated in December 2023 the California Secretary of
  Transportation visited Malibu and toured PCH with City staff and other Caltrans
  officials. He stated the Secretary shared that he had committed $4.25 million
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 8, 2024
  Page 5 of 12

  dollars for improvements on PCH in Malibu. He stated the City had a PCH Safety
  webpage that was regularly updated with infomation from all relevant agencies.
  He stated staffwas working on a long-term contract with California Highway Patrol
  (CHP) for enforcement on PCH. He stated staff had requested modifications to the
  contract and they were being reviewed by legal teams in Sacramento. He reported
  on other recent accidents on PCH. He announced a screening of 21 Miles in Malibu
  on January 18, 2024. He announced the Homeless Count on January 24, 2024 and
  stated volunteers were still needed. He announced a City Council Study Session
  on the Draft Housing Element on January l7, 2024. He stated the Temporary Use
  Permit (TUP) Ordinance was scheduled for the February 12, 2024 City Council
  meeting.

  Captain Jennifer Seetoo, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, discussed a
  fatal accident in Malibu and stated detectives did not believe that accident was
  caused by speed. She discussed a speeding incident on December 28, 2023 where
  the suspect was driving over 100 mph. She discussed joint operations with CHP.
  She discussed the importance of adding speed cameras in the City. She discussed
  the importance of focusing on school safety in addition to PCH safety. She stated
  the School Safety Sergent would be returning later this month and she planned to
  meet with the mother of a school shooter who educated the public on this issue.
  She stated the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department was partnering with the
  Las Virgenes School District to add their public facing cameras to the real time
  crime system. She stated she looked forward to partnering with the City and Santa
  Monica-Malibu Unified School District on more school safety efforts.

  Mayor Uhring stated the City’s lobbyist California Strategies was working on a
  draft bill to permit speed cameras in Malibu and the draft would be provided to
  Senator Ben Allen by January 18, 2024. He requested Captain Seetoo provide
  statistics on the number of speeding tickets issued to the City so that information
  could be conveyed to California Strategies.

  Scott Dittrich, Public Works Commission, stated that since the accident on PCH
  that killed four Pepperdine students, the Commission had been focusing on aspects
  of Public Works that can be used to enhance safety. He discussed Public Works
  Director DuBoux’s efforts to work with Caltrans on PCH improvements. He
  discussed the broken windows theory and recommended focusing on minor
  violations such as excessive noise, in addition to speeding Violations.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Grisanti stated he enjoyed the holidays and spoke to a lot of
  residents. He encouraged everyone to obey the speed limit.

  Councilmember Riggins stated she received positive feedback from the employees
  about the winter holiday closure. She stated she attended a League of California
  Cities event last week on the zero bail policy. She announced a volunteer weed
  pulling event at Point Dume Headlands on January 10, 2024.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of January 8, 2024
  Page 6 of 12

  Councilmember Silverstein thanked the public speakers and those who submitted
  written comments. He stated he had spent a lot of time on research for Item No.
  7.A. and on understanding issues related to the farmer’s market. He stated he spoke
  with Supervisor Horvath on both issues. He stated he had been conscientiously
  driving the speed limit and stated many people were speeding, including in
  construction zones.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart encouraged everyone to set the pace on PCH by obeying
  the speed limit. He discussed the meeting with the Secretary of Transportation and
  stated he learned that in California speed limits were determined based on the actual
  speed of drivers. He stated it was important to encourage slower driving so the
  speed limit on PCH could be lowered. He recommended the Public Safety and
  Public Works Commissions have more joint meetings to work on PCH safety items.
  He stated he attended a PCH Task Force meeting, and the PCH tour with the
  Secretary of Transportation. He stated the PCH tour was planned at the direction
  ofthe Governor’s office and included many high-level officials from the State. He
  stated he attended a meeting with California Strategies and discussed the bill to
  approve speed cameras in Malibu. He discussed the challenges to get the bill
  approved and the limitations of the bill.

  Mayor Uhring indicated agreement with all the comments about the importance of
  limiting speeding on PCH. He stated he enjoyed the holidays.

  Mayor Pro Tem Stewart discussed The Malibu Times articles on PCH safety and
  thanked them for their support on the issue. He thanked Hans Laetz for covering
  the issues on KBUU.

  In response to Mayor Uhring, the Councilmembers indicated that they intended to
  complete the agenda tonight and hear Item No. 7.A.
